description: Manage working trees that share one Git repository.

options.detail: --help-all also prints built-in usage. Immediately after worktree, --help opens the Git manual viewer.
Supply PATH and optionally BRANCH or COMMIT. With no start point, Git uses a branch named after the last path component, creating it at HEAD if needed. Each worktree has its own HEAD and index.

options.summary: List the main and linked worktrees
options.detail: The main worktree appears first, followed by linked worktrees and their branch or detached state.
Removes its files and registration. The main worktree cannot be removed.
Use when the working directory is already gone. For a directory moved by hand, use worktree repair to reconnect it.

options.summary: Protect a linked worktree while its directory is unavailable
options.detail: Supply WORKTREE, optionally with --reason TEXT. A lock protects the registration from pruning and restricts moving or removing the worktree.
Supply WORKTREE. Its registration becomes eligible for ordinary pruning, moving and removal.

options.summary: Move a linked worktree to a new path
options.detail: Supply WORKTREE NEW-PATH. The main worktree and worktrees with submodules cannot be moved here. A locked worktree needs --force twice. Git 2.53 and upstream also accept --[no-]relative-paths.

options.summary: Reconnect worktrees after a manual move
options.detail: Run in the moved worktree, or supply the new paths from the main repository. Git 2.53 and upstream can rewrite link paths with --relative-paths or --no-relative-paths.
